verdict.reasoning: Patient reports upper-lip swelling that is progressing after prawn soup: "there is like a swelling on my, on my upper lip and it's kind of getting bigger" and this followed eating a prawn soup.

Timing and progression match: prawn soup "just after work, so maybe like around seven" and swelling developed in "like, I don't know half an hour maybe," with current description that it's "kinda getting bigger."

Patient says "I feel like I can't breathe that well right now" and later "I feel a little dizzy right now to be honest," and is unsure about chest: "it just generally feels a little difficult, but yeah it might be, I'm not sure."

Transcript: past episode after late night Chinese curry with swelling and difficult breathing, but no statement that it self-resolved after salbutamol or that salbutamol was used for that episode: "I remember that after like having that very late... I've woke up the next morning quite swollen up and had also I, felt really bad and quite difficult breathing"; salbutamol is discussed only as regular asthma medication.
Patient explicitly: "I generally have asthma" and repeats this.

Peanut allergy and severe childhood reaction described: "I have a peanut allergy as well, like always had it" and doctor asks about hospital for severe reaction; patient: "Yeah is that well I was like six or something..." implying severe past reaction needing hospital and injection.

Transcript notes temporal association with prawn soup but no explicit statement of a new shellfish allergy: "I ordered a prawn soup... now I feel... there is a swelling"; "Possible new allergy to shellfish" is an interpretive addition beyond what is stated.
Patient says they take salbutamol regularly: "I took I, I take, ohh what's it called? Salbutamol inhalers?... I do take that regularly"; no mention that it is used only "as needed."
Patient: "I do sometimes but I don't know which ones" when asked about antihistamines and notes they get antihistamines for peanut allergy but is unsure of type.
Mother is present or reachable, but living arrangement is not stated. Patient later calls out "Mum, Mum do we have any antihistamines around?"; this does not confirm they live together.

Upper-lip swelling is reported by the patient but there is no documentation that the clinician visually observed edema: "now I feel the that there is a swelling... on my upper lip"; video observation is not explicitly stated.
Dyspnea and dizziness are patient-reported: "I feel like I can't breathe that well right now" and later "I feel a little dizzy right now to be honest."

Doctor explicitly suspects anaphylaxis linked to prawn (shellfish) ingestion with lip and airway symptoms: "it sounds like you could be going into what we say an a, an anaphylactic reaction. That's when your throat and your chest, you know closes in"; this follows acute lip swelling after prawn soup and breathing difficulty.

Baseline asthma is stated: "I generally have asthma" and only salbutamol inhaler is used: "I took... Salbutamol inhalers?... I do take that regularly" and "no I don't think so" to any other (brown) inhalers, consistent with SABA-only regimen.

History of severe peanut reaction is described: peanut allergy plus childhood hospital/injection event: doctor asks about injection and hospital; patient confirms an event around age six that required hospital: "Yeah is that well I was like six or something" in the context of severe allergic reaction.

Doctor directs emergency ambulance call to 999: "I think we need to call an ambulance" and later instructs mother "call the uh nine nine , nine nine nine yeah, and say that your there is a suspected anaphylactic reaction and they need to come straight away."

Doctor instructs use of available antihistamines while waiting: "Could you ask the person whether they have any antihistamines around, in the interim, while we're waiting" and later "so straight away take the antihistamines in the meantime."
Doctor ensures companion stays: "is there any, anyone with you at the moment or are you alone?... make sure that person's with you till the ambulance comes."

Future plan only mentions possible injections and follow-up, not specific prescriptions or allergy referral: "we might need to sort you out, um, with your injections and things like that"; no explicit mention of adrenaline autoinjector or allergy clinic referral.
Transcript does not mention reviewing asthma control, adding ICS, or an asthma action plan at follow-up; this is not discussed.
